analyticalQuestion: How much extra many-carrier suppression follows from the exact target-row norm, and do one-carrier Bessel roots occur before the adjacent frozen-profile enhanced-dissipation scale?
takeaway: For the canonical exact-launch profile r_l=l,z_l=1, chi_M=1/(2M) and Omega^2/Kv is asymptotic to 12/M. With M/Ks asymptotic to 3/M^2, the normalized geometric prefactor is M^-10/3 and the sufficient phase boundary is alpha<min(5/2,(10+3beta)/7). The one-carrier Bessel layer remains earlier than the frozen-profile enhanced-dissipation comparison scale.
palettePolicy: one muted blue root plus one ochre focus and neutral references
nonColorEncoding: filled circles, open squares, and open triangles
fixed panel order from phase boundary to geometric factors to Bessel diagnostics

panels.A: old, target-participation, and coherent sufficient phase boundaries
panels.B: equal-carrier chi, Omega squared over Kv, and combined gain
panels.C: Bessel short-layer enhanced-dissipation, heat-freezing, and energy-loss indicators

claimBoundary: Panels A and B use analytic formulas. Panel C evaluates analytic comparison formulas at Bessel zeros. Producer and independent calculations are deterministic but not interval arithmetic. A positive burn-in can control only the remaining tail ledger and cannot remove pre-burn-in slope mass. The figure does not construct a normalized lower family, perform DNS, or prove Navier-Stokes regularity or blow-up.
